summary: An NGS data sheet gives a 1966 Coast and Geodetic Survey description of the Benton County fire tower: 110 feet (33.5 m) tall, a metal cab on a skeleton structure; no source found gives its current status.

facts.design: Metal cab on a four-legged skeleton structure

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed and described the station in 1966. The sheet gives no build date for the tower.
Condition report in the NGS history rates the survey station GOOD. It does not say whether the tower stands.

notes_for_editor: Two sources, both quoting the same 1966 survey description, so the physical details rest on one document. The sheet names the Mississippi Forest Service as owner, while its road sign reads Mississippi Forestry Commission-Benton; the story states both. No current status, access or staffing found. The Benton County wildfire plan (2020 PDF) mentions no lookout tower. The record point (34.95233, -89.03258) was not checked against the sheet's directions (11 miles SE of Grand Junction, Tennessee; 7.5 miles W of Walnut). The NGS history also logs a 2009 GOOD condition report for the station; the story cites it and notes that it does not say whether the tower stands.
